name: Nebo
title: Babylonian deity mentioned in the Bible
summary: Nebo (also spelled Nabu) is not a biblical figure but a Babylonian god mentioned in the Bible, especially in the writings of the prophet Isaiah. He was the god of wisdom and writing in the Babylonian pantheon, son of Marduk (Merodach). His name also appears as part of Babylonian royal names such as Nebuchadnezzar and Nabu-sharrussu-ukin, and in the Bible references to Nebo are used to show God's superiority over idols.

keyEvents.title: Nebo Bows Down
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah describes how the Babylonian idols Bel and Nebo will bow down and fall, unable to save themselves, in contrast to Israel's living God.

keyEvents.title: God's Superiority Over Idols
keyEvents.description: In the same context, God declares that He is the one who carries His people, unlike the idols which must be carried by humans.

keyEvents.title: Nebo as a Place Name – Mount Nebo
keyEvents.description: Nebo is also the name of the mountain from which Moses saw the Promised Land before he died. Mount Nebo is located in Moab and is an important site in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Nebo as a City in Moab
keyEvents.description: Nebo is mentioned as a city in the land of Moab that was captured by the Israelites and later referred to by the prophets in oracles of judgment against Moab.

keyEvents.title: Men from Nebo in the Return from Exile
keyEvents.description: After the Babylonian exile, men from the town of Nebo are mentioned among those who returned to Judah, as well as some from Nebo who had taken foreign wives.
